hypothesis: A small forward neck target shift improves forward sprint speed or higher-command controllability without new native failures.
sign: Negative MuJoCo neck angle moves head/neck COM forward; verified static sensitivity.
gate: active skill sprint and requested vx>0; linear move_toward applied once per50Hz decision; ramp to zero on exit; reset immediately to zero on reset
action_contract: offset added to inferred action[5] as bias_rad/action_scale before control conversion; record raw policy output and final executed action; next observation uses final executed action
variant_selection: Each fixed variant evaluated once at both speeds; no tuning of angle/ramp after seeing results.
signal: At0.30:32/32,no falls,and paired long net forward speed >=baseline*1.05, or at0.45: >=baseline passes+4,no new failed courses,no falls,and no net-speed regression. Required posture/COM change measured; no marginal speed-only promotion.
acceptance: Screening only. Before default promotion require paired ordinary control/no regression, final held-out seeds and real host controls; no default installation on a partial screen.
resource_limit: two native workers, two CPU affinity cores,nice10; no training or additional GPU simulation; user and other-agent processes never killed
